title: Trace stallcheck debug diary
content:
Context:
Observed intermittent 30-60m gaps in trace ingestion for service set A (payment*, checkout). Metrics show span count dropping to near zero while application traffic continued. This doc is my scratchpad for commands, evidence, quick hypotheses and next steps. Notes to self, messy — intended for me and anyone I ping on-call.

Summary of symptoms (seen 2026-03-09 22:10 -> 2026-03-09 23:05 UTC):
- Spans emitted from instrumented services (opentelemetry) but collector shows very low receive_rate.
- Kafka topic obs-traces had consumer lag spike then fall to zero with consumer group rebalancing.
- Vector (collector) logs include repeated warnings about TLS write errors and occasional "batch write timeout".
- Metrics pipeline (Prometheus remote write) unaffected -> suggests issue is in trace path specifically.

Quick evidence snippets (raw lines captured):
- vector logs (kubectl -n observability logs deploy/vector-collector -c vector):
  "WARN vector::sinks::kafka: Failed to produce records: error=\"Failed to send batch: Broken pipe\""
  "ERROR vector::topology: Batch write timeout after 30s, dropping batch id=5982"
- kafka broker logs (grep on broker-2):
  "WARN ReplicaFetch(consumer) request timed out, disconnecting"
- trace-indexer (consumer) stderr: \"Consumer heartbeat failed: rebalance in progress; processed=0\"
- app side (service checkout) OTLP exporter: \"WARN exporter: failed to export spans: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed\"

Commands I ran / immediate checks (timestamps are local to when I ran):
- Check consumer groups: 
  kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group trace-indexers  # saw REBALANCING and then 0 members briefly
- Tail vector logs: 
  kubectl -n observability logs -l app=vector-collector -c vector --since=2h | sed -n '1,200p'
- Inspect pod resource pressure: 
  kubectl top pod vector-collector-5f7d -n observability; kubectl describe pod vector-collector-5f7d
- Check node dmesg for OOM or throttling: 
  ssh node-8 sudo dmesg | tail -n 200
- Capture tcpdump between app and collector for 1 minute: 
  kubectl exec -n observability -it vector-collector-5f7d -- tcpdump -i any port 4317 -w /tmp/otlp.pcap & sleep 60; pkill -f tcpdump; kubectl cp observability/vector-collector-5f7d:/tmp/otlp.pcap ./otlp.pcap
- Check JVM exporter events (for indexer): 
  kubectl logs -n observability trace-indexer-0 | grep -i "rebalance\|heartbeat\|exception"

Things I observed during those checks:
- No OOMs on node, but CPU from vector pod was pegged at ~90% for a short period during the gap window.
- tcpdump shows short bursts of OTLP traffic from apps, then no packets from collector to kafka for the same window -> suggests collector accepted some spans then stalled writing to kafka.
- vector config has batch.timeout_ms = 30000 and batch.max_bytes = 4_194_304 (4MB) — if downstream Kafka is slow, batches will sit.
- Kafka broker metrics show leader under-replicated partitions for topic obs-traces around the time (not massive, but non-zero).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Downstream Kafka broker slow/unavailable causing vector to block on produce and then fail batches; consumer group rebalancing and indexing sees zero because messages never committed.
2) Recent deploy changed vector config or OTLP exporter sampling -> sampling dropped to 0 for a subset of services. (Less likely because multiple services affected and tcpdump shows OTLP packets from apps.)
3) TLS handshake issues between vector and Kafka (library-level error shows Broken pipe) possibly due to cert rotation or MTU issues.
4) Consumer group (trace-indexer) is flapping due to GC pauses or thread pool starvation, causing frequent rebalances and therefore lag.
5) Network packet drops between collector and kafka (cilium policy change or loadbalancer hit).

Immediate mitigation attempts (what I did):
- Restarted vector deployment (kubectl rollout restart deploy/vector-collector -n observability) -> short-term improvement, spans flowed for ~6 minutes then dropped again.
- Scaled replica count from 2 -> 4 for vector -> reduced per-pod CPU and stopped immediate batch timeouts, but issue recurred after ~40 minutes.
- Manually triggered kafka preferred leader election for obs-traces partition 0 (kafka-preferred-replica-election.sh) -> minor improvement in broker metrics.

Evidence ruling out some hypotheses:
- Sampling config unchanged in git (checked last PRs) and app OTLP shows spans emitted -> hypothesis 2 unlikely.
- No certificate rotation events in cert-manager logs around the times -> TLS cert rotation less likely but still possible if intermediate network device interferes.

Next data to collect (todo):
- Capture long tcpdump between vector pod and kafka for full incident window and check retransmits/ICMP.
- Increase vector log level to trace for 30 minutes and forward to a temporary debug topic so we don't drop them.
- Enable Java GC logging on trace-indexer to check for long pauses.
- Run kafka producer tool against broker during incident to test produce latency: 
  kafka-producer-perf-test.sh --throughput -1 --producer-props bootstrap.servers=kafka:9092 --topic obs-traces --num-records 10000 --record-size 1024
- Run netstat/lsof in vector pod during incident to confirm open sockets and any ESTABLISHED -> TIME_WAIT patterns.

Quick checklist for next pager run (what to try):
- If spans stop: immediately run kafka-consumer-groups.sh and kubectl logs on vector; check vector metrics: vector_transmission_failures_total and vector_sink_send_latency_seconds.
- If vector shows "Broken pipe" errors, attempt rolling restart of brokers and vector simultaneously to break stale TLS sessions.
- If producer latencies > 5s, escalate to infra (kafka cluster owners).

Who to ping:
- @Liam (kafka) - broker health and replication concerns
- @Jordan (vector) - config, batch settings, upgrade PRs
- @SRE on-call - if this becomes >= 30m continuous gap

Open questions / weirdness to follow up on:
- Why did restart temporarily fix it? (Transient backlog cleared?)
- Why did scale to 4 replicas not permanently fix? (Maybe global broker pressure still causes intermittent blocking)
- Are restarts causing flapping consumer groups that worsen stability? Need graceful drain.

Notes to self: keep trace of any manual leader elections and restarts in the incident ticket before doing more changes. If we decide to increase batch.timeout, coordinate with product for possible data loss risk.

Appendix - useful commands (copyable):
- kafka consumer group: kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group trace-indexers
- check vector pod logs: kubectl -n observability logs -l app=vector-collector -c vector --since=1h | grep -i "error\|warn" -n | sed -n '1,200p'
- capture tcpdump: kubectl exec -n observability vector-collector-5f7d -- tcpdump -i any host kafka-broker-2 -w /tmp/debug.pcap & sleep 120; pkill -f tcpdump
- list open sockets: kubectl exec -n observability vector-collector-5f7d -- ss -tunap | head -n 200

End of scratchpad. Will keep appending as I iterate.

Signature: Ava M. (notes, not authoritative)
